key_insight: The paper develops a dimension-independent theory showing that fractional parabolic PDE solutions can be efficiently approximated by neural networks using anisotropic spectral Barron spaces that separate time and space regularity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theoretical foundation for scalable neural solvers for high-dimensional fractional diffusion models with drift and potential terms, with provable approximation rates.
method: Introduce anisotropic spectral Barron spaces to measure temporal and spatial frequency regularity separately.
Prove dimension-independent maximal regularity using multiplication estimates and the method of continuity.
Use a Vandermonde-based global-in-time extension of the fractional heat semigroup to analyze forward evolution in space-time Fourier variables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical approximation guarantees, including n^{-1/2} two-layer network bounds in mixed Sobolev norms under specified activation and regularity conditions.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees depend on anisotropic Barron regularity assumptions, and uniform-in-time spectral Barron regularity can fail in general.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation of Solutions to Fractional Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
